heading: Saved service fields
body: A service field marked @SessionState is saved in sessionStorage for the life of the tab. A field marked @LocalState is saved in localStorage, so it comes back in later visits on this device. Both markers work in JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Java, C#, F#, Rust, Go, Ruby, Python and Lua services. A Python field writes the marker in its type, as `Annotated[str, session_state]`. A Lua field writes the marker as a comment line above it, as `-- @SessionState`. One field takes one of the two markers, and never together with Needs. The old `$` and `$$` field prefixes are refused, and the message names the marker to write. `ty migrate fix --write` changes the fields, their uses in the class and in the views, and a value saved under the old key moves to the new key once. Tachyon restores saved values before OnStart runs. Each assignment stores JSON of up to 64 KiB. A larger value is not saved: the assignment throws a RangeError that names the key, the size and the limit, and the field keeps its last value. When a service method sets such a value, the method throws (or its promise rejects) and the saved copy keeps its last value. Keep large data in a Store table. When a service method changes its own saved field, the new value is saved as the method returns; this is also true for a Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java or Ruby service that runs as WebAssembly. The same holds for a service that only another service needs, such as a NotesService that an EditorService holds in a Needs field. Its saved fields keep the key `tac:service:<instance>:<page path>:<field>`, whether a view uses the service, another service needs it, or both, so the two uses never disagree. This works in JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Go, Java, F#, Python and C++, the languages whose browser services can need another service; the Needs field in each of them is shown under "A service that needs another service: Tac". Rust, Kotlin, Swift and C# browser services cannot need another service (TY1406, TY1308), and neither can Ruby and Lua services (TY2015). A Rust service linked into a native app that another Rust service holds through `Arc` is saved too; declare its saved field as `std::sync::Mutex<T>` or `std::sync::RwLock<T>`, because `Arc` gives shared access only (ADR 0119). To save a change inside the value, assign the field again. Template handlers and OnEvent methods render the view again automatically. Background work uses an injected taskScheduler. If the browser denies storage or its quota (storage limit) is full, the UI still works. Never save secrets.
